 Leveraging the role of the capital city based on Hanoi's practical experience to contribute to the improvement of policies and laws.
 On the afternoon of October 15th, the Hanoi City National Assembly delegation held a working session with the Standing Committee of the People's Council, the People's Committee, and the Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee of Hanoi City in preparation for the second session of the 16th National Assembly.
 Hà Nội Mới • 15/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 General Secretary and President To Lam and National Assembly delegates from Hanoi attend the working session. Photo: Quang Thai. Attending the working session were: General Secretary and President To Lam; Politburo member, Secretary of the Hanoi City Party Committee, and Head of the Hanoi City National Assembly Delegation Tran Duc Thang ; Central Committee member, Deputy Secretary of the Hanoi City Party Committee, and Chairman of the Hanoi City People's Committee Vu Dai Thang; and Deputy Secretary of the Hanoi City Party Committee, Chairwoman of the Hanoi City People's Council, and Deputy Head of the Hanoi City National Assembly Delegation Phung Thi Hong Ha. 
 General Secretary and President To Lam and National Assembly delegates from Hanoi. Photo: Quang Thai Also attending were National Assembly delegates from the Hanoi delegation; and leaders of various departments and agencies of the city.
 Eight groups of tasks and solutions to realize the 16.55% growth target in the fourth quarter. 
 Reporting on solutions to ensure the achievement of the city's 2026 growth target, Standing Committee member of the City Party Committee and Vice Chairman of the Hanoi People's Committee Nguyen Xuan Luu stated that in the third quarter of 2026, the city recorded a breakthrough with a growth rate of 10.02%, higher than the national average for the third quarter (9.95%). This is the first time this year that Hanoi has achieved double-digit growth, and also the highest growth rate in any quarter. The estimated GRDP growth for the first nine months reached 8.85%, higher than the 7.92% of the same period in 2025. State budget revenue by September 30, 2026 reached VND 568,585 billion, equivalent to 87.5% of the projected amount, an increase of 6.1% compared to the same period… 
 Vice Chairman of Hanoi People's Committee Nguyen Xuan Luu reports at the working session. Photo: Quang Thai The city continues to implement Directive No. 17/CT-UBND dated July 23, 2026, of the Chairman of the People's Committee of the city, updating the Q4 scenario based on the results of Q3 and the first nine months, steadfastly maintaining the GRDP growth target for the whole year without downward adjustment. Accordingly, the city has developed a Q4 growth scenario of 16.55%.
 To achieve its growth targets, the city will implement eight key tasks and solutions in the remaining months of the year. Specifically, these include accelerating public investment, construction volume, and key projects; promoting industrial production, exports, and new production capacity; stimulating trade, consumption, tourism, transportation, and services; facilitating credit, private investment, and the real estate market; promoting science and technology, innovation, and digital transformation ; controlling prices, input costs, and protecting purchasing power; resolving issues related to land clearance, resettlement, and technical infrastructure; and tightening accountability in implementation and monitoring growth based on results.
 78 legal documents have been issued to implement the Law on the Capital City. 
 Regarding the assessment of the specific implementation of the assigned powers in the 2026 Capital City Law and the initial evaluation of how these mechanisms and policies are being put into practice, Vice Chairman of the Hanoi People's Committee Nguyen Xuan Luu stated that, even during the drafting of the Capital City Law, the Hanoi People's Committee proactively prepared the conditions for organizing the implementation of the Law, adhering to the principle that lawmaking must be linked to law enforcement. 
 Delegates attending the working session. Photo: Quang Thai The concretization of the powers of the Capital City Law has been implemented by the City People's Committee on a broad scale, involving many areas of state management such as organizational structure, investment, finance and budget, planning, urban development, land, environment, science and technology, innovation, digital transformation, education , health, culture, and social security... The documents developed focus on the contents of the Capital City Law that the City People's Council and People's Committee are tasked with specifying or, within their authority, concretizing specific mechanisms and policies to be implemented in the city.
 To date, the City People's Council has issued 61 normative legal resolutions implementing the Law on the Capital City, and the City People's Committee has issued 17 normative legal decisions implementing the Law on the Capital City. Along with issuing new documents, the City People's Committee has reviewed the current system of normative legal documents to ensure consistency and uniformity when the Law on the Capital City in 2026 comes into effect. Based on the results of this review, the City People's Committee submitted to the City People's Council for promulgation Resolution No. 23/NQ-HĐND dated June 2, 2026, announcing 22 normative legal resolutions detailing the Law on the Capital City in 2024 that will continue to be in effect; and issued Decision No. 2849/QĐ-UBND dated June 6, 2026, announcing 2 normative legal decisions detailing the Law on the Capital City in 2024 that will continue to be in effect.
 Through the initial implementation phase, several mechanisms and policies have been put into practice, creating a legal basis and resources to support citizens, businesses, scientific organizations, and educational institutions, while also promoting the areas the city has identified as priorities.
 In terms of science, technology, innovation, and digital transformation, the city has initially implemented mechanisms for allocating funds and supporting scientific, technological, and innovation tasks; some tasks have been approved and implemented under a cost-sharing mechanism linked to the type of task and output results. Regarding controlled testing mechanisms, the city has approved two projects, including a project on autonomous intelligent transportation and a project on rare earth oxide production, thereby initially putting the mechanism for testing new technologies into practice.
 The city has also implemented mechanisms to mobilize resources, established funds, support institutions, and an Innovation Center; and has begun to implement policies to support digital transformation and synthesize the needs of beneficiaries. In addition, cooperation between the government, research institutions, educational institutions, and businesses has been promoted in several areas such as quantum technology, semiconductors, new materials, high-tech human resource training, and applied research.
 Regarding education, healthcare, culture, and social welfare, several new policies and mechanisms, in accordance with resolutions of the City People's Council, have been implemented, focusing on supporting citizens, developing human resources, improving the quality of public services, and ensuring social security. The initial implementation has had a direct impact on several beneficiary groups, while also providing a foundation for the city to implement policies that are appropriate to the development requirements in the new situation.
 Regarding organizational structure, decentralization, urban management, investment, land, environment, and other areas of state management, the mechanisms assigned to the city by the Capital City Law and its implementing documents are gradually being concretized, contributing to a clearer understanding of the responsibilities and authority of agencies in carrying out their tasks. The implementation of new regulations also initially creates a basis for the city to be more proactive in management, administration, addressing practical needs, and mobilizing resources for development.

 Bui Huyen Mai, Chairwoman of the Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee of Hanoi City, presents a report at the working session. Photo: Quang Thai. Ms. Bui Huyen Mai, Member of the Standing Committee of the Hanoi City Party Committee and Chairwoman of the Vietnam Fatherland Front Committee of Hanoi City, presented a summary of the opinions and recommendations of voters to the second session of the 16th National Assembly. Representatives from the Hanoi City People's Court and the Hanoi City People's Procuracy presented a summary of their work results for the first nine months of 2026, the direction and tasks for the last three months of 2026, and recommendations from their respective sectors to the second session of the 16th National Assembly.
 Continue to make in-depth contributions to the success of the National Assembly session.
 Speaking at the meeting, General Secretary and President To Lam said that, based on the opinions of voters compiled by the National Assembly delegation of the city during the voter consultation meeting before the second session of the 16th National Assembly, voters trust and support the major decisions and directives of the Party and the State in the past period. 
 General Secretary and President To Lam speaks at the working session. Photo: Quang Thai During the working session, the General Secretary and President emphasized the need to concretize the Party's policies, improve governance capacity, and enhance national development. The National Assembly delegation from the city should study draft laws within the overall policy framework, ensuring favorable investment regulations are supported by legislation; assigning additional tasks to local authorities must take into account their authority and the necessary conditions for implementation; and clarifying any overlaps between laws, levels, and sectors to ensure transparency and prevent delays due to unclear responsibility.
 General Secretary and President To Lam emphasized the need to improve the quality of legislation and ensure the legitimate rights and interests of the people in the development process. Regarding land, housing, real estate business, investment, and bidding projects, it is necessary to resolve the obstacles that have emerged in practice. Policies must facilitate production and business while ensuring fairness and strict management of public resources.
 The General Secretary and President requested that all regulations be considered in terms of both their impact on the people and the ability of responsible agencies to implement them. Voters in Hanoi have reported many cases of long-term land use with incomplete documentation and slow procedures for issuing land certificates. We need to review the mechanism for verifying the origin and history of land use to ensure it is based on evidence and in accordance with the law. 
 General Secretary and President To Lam speaks at the working session. Photo: Quang Thai General Secretary and President To Lam stated that policies on land prices and financial obligations must be transparent and take into account practical impacts. Land acquisition must be linked to the process of preparing for resettlement and restoring livelihoods, paying attention to the elderly and middle-aged who face difficulties in changing occupations; at the same time, early dialogue should be organized to limit disputes later. To resolve outstanding projects, it is necessary to classify the causes, handle them according to authority, and protect the legitimate interests of all parties. Violations should not be legalized, and losses should not be shifted to innocent parties. Housing development must pay close attention to supply that matches affordability, including social housing and long-term rental housing.
 Long-term investment businesses need property rights that are protected and consistent policies that are enforced. It is necessary to prevent the re-establishment of business conditions in guidelines or the shifting of inter-agency obligations onto businesses. Projects related to healthcare, insurance, education, and food safety must be considered from the perspective of the beneficiaries' needs. Insurance benefits must be linked to the availability of medicines and services; educational policies must have adequate schools and teachers; food safety management must be traceable, with clear accountability, especially for school meals. Related policies with varying effects must be handled fairly during the transition period.
 Regarding criminal law, procedural law, the organization of investigative agencies, and the fight against crime, it must be linked to protecting human rights, preventing wrongful convictions, and controlling power. For the proposed pilot program to recover and handle assets related to crimes committed without conviction, the basis, authority, procedures, and the right to litigation must be clearly defined, along with a mechanism for reviewing the rights of bona fide third parties. The new policy needs thorough explanation regarding its legal guarantees.
 General Secretary and President To Lam proposed that decisions on budget plans should aim for high growth while maintaining stability and improving the people's living standards.
 The General Secretary and President emphasized the need to leverage the role of the capital city, drawing on Hanoi's practical experience, to contribute to the improvement of general policies and laws.
 Emphasizing the need to continue monitoring results and tracking the fulfillment of commitments to voters, General Secretary and President To Lam requested the Hanoi City National Assembly Delegation to uphold the responsibility of the delegation and each delegate towards the issues facing the capital city.
 General Secretary and President To Lam expressed his confidence that the Hanoi City National Assembly delegation would continue to make profound contributions to the success of the National Assembly session.
 Gain a thorough understanding of the realities of the capital city to effectively serve activities in the National Assembly.
 Concluding the working session, Tran Duc Thang, Secretary of the Hanoi City Party Committee and Head of the Hanoi City National Assembly Delegation, stated that the directives and guidance from the General Secretary and President serve as encouragement and inspiration, while also placing responsibilities on each National Assembly delegate from the capital city. 
 You may also like Secretary of the Hanoi City Party Committee and Head of the Hanoi City National Assembly Delegation, Tran Duc Thang, delivered the concluding remarks at the working session. According to Party Secretary Tran Duc Thang, through reports and discussions, National Assembly delegates unanimously agreed on the achievements of the Party Committee, government, and people of Hanoi in the past nine months; they also acknowledged the difficulties and obstacles that the city is currently focusing on resolving and need to make further efforts in implementation.
 According to Comrade Tran Duc Thang, at the first session and the first extraordinary session of the 16th National Assembly, the Hanoi City National Assembly Delegation clearly demonstrated a sense of responsibility. The city's National Assembly delegates delivered 179 speeches in committee and plenary sessions. The delegation contributed opinions on 47 draft laws and resolutions with 59 written comments, ensuring deadlines were met. Many of the delegation's opinions were incorporated by the National Assembly, the Government, and the drafting agencies during the project completion process. The delegation's oversight activities closely followed the Party's guidelines, the National Assembly's oversight program, and the political tasks of the Capital City. 
 Delegates attending the working session. Photo: Quang Thai The City Party Secretary stated that the second session of the 16th National Assembly, starting on October 17th, will require the timely institutionalization of the Party's decisions into law in accordance with the guiding principles and with feasibility. The General Secretary and President have repeatedly emphasized the value of these decisions, demonstrated through the solutions implemented and the positive changes in people's lives. Leading localities must play a leading role; this is a direct requirement for the legislative, supervisory, and decision-making activities of the National Assembly, and a responsibility of each National Assembly delegate from the city. Therefore, the City's National Assembly delegation hopes that the delegates will continue to closely monitor and understand the realities of the capital city to support their activities in the second session of the National Assembly. 
 Scene from the working session. Photo: Quang Thai The City Party Secretary also requested the Standing Committee of the People's Council, the People's Committee, the Fatherland Front Committee, the People's Court, the People's Procuratorate, and the city's departments and agencies to fully incorporate the opinions of the National Assembly deputies in order to more decisively implement the issues of concern to the deputies and voters. They should continue to effectively coordinate the implementation of the coordination regulations, create favorable conditions for National Assembly deputies to carry out their duties and powers, and pay attention to the implementation of several key tasks that have been emphasized by the General Secretary and the President.
 “The delegation of National Assembly representatives from the city respectfully thanks and fully absorbs all the contents, especially the guiding principles of the General Secretary and the President, to participate in the upcoming second session. The delegation will closely coordinate with relevant agencies to seriously implement the plan with the highest goal of building a cultured, civilized, modern, and happy capital city, improving people's lives, and ensuring social justice,” Comrade Tran Duc Thang emphasized.
 On this occasion, the Secretary of the City Party Committee and Head of the National Assembly Delegation of the city, Tran Duc Thang, expressed his gratitude to the National Assembly delegates, city agencies, voters, and the people for their support and contributions in ensuring that parliamentary activities closely reflect the realities of life.
